summary: The Hotel Fees Transparency Act of 2025 requires hotels, short-term rentals, and online booking platforms to clearly display the total price of a room—including both the base price and mandatory service fees—whenever they advertise prices. It also requires the disclosure of government-imposed taxes and fees prior to final purchase, provides enforcement mechanisms through the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, and preempts inconsistent state laws.

affected_groups.effect: Will see total upfront pricing including mandatory service fees when shopping for hotels or short-term rentals.
Must alter advertising and pricing displays to prominently feature total service prices rather than base prices alone.
Must integrate total pricing displays into their platforms and platforms can utilize an affirmative defense if they relied in good faith on incorrect data from lodging providers.
Gains enforcement authority to penalize deceptive advertising practices and bring civil actions on behalf of state residents.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Requires covered entities to display the total services price (base price plus mandatory service fees) anywhere a price is advertised, marketed, or listed.
Mandates that the total services price be disclosed when lodging services are first shown to a buyer and at all times throughout the purchasing process.
Requires disclosure of any government or quasi-government taxes, fees, or assessments prior to the final purchase.
Allows third-party intermediaries and online sellers to display individual price components or optional add-ons, provided they are less prominent than the total price.
Provides an affirmative defense for third-party sellers who relied in good faith on inaccurate pricing information provided by a hotel or short-term rental.
Enforces violations through the Federal Trade Commission under the Federal Trade Commission Act and allows state attorneys general or authorized state officials to bring civil actions.
Preempts state and local laws regarding short-term lodging price displays and fee disclosures unless they match the requirement to include service fees in the total services price.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for potential civil penalties or fines for violations.
Exact budgetary impact or administrative costs for the Federal Trade Commission.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Hotel Fees Transparency Act of 2025 requires hotels, short-term rentals, and online booking platforms to clearly display the total price of a room—including both the base price and mandatory service fees—whenever they advertise prices. It also requires the disclosure of government-imposed taxes and fees prior to final purchase, provides enforcement mechanisms through the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, and preempts inconsistent state laws.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a nationwide standard for short-term lodging price transparency by requiring mandatory fees to be included in initial price displays. This changes how the hospitality and online booking industries market rooms, preempts differing state advertising regulations, and empowers both federal regulators and state officials to enforce compliance.
